transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for being here. As we prepare to finalize the graduation ceremony plan for June 12 at the civic auditorium, I'd like each of you to report any information that must be reflected in the plan before I give my final approval. Please go ahead and share what you know — registrar, facilities coordinator, family liaison, and counselor, what do each of you have for me?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag an important update regarding diplomas. I completed the credit audit this morning, and it shows that exactly seven seniors are still short of graduation requirements and therefore cannot receive diplomas at the ceremony. These results have not yet been entered into the ceremony roster, so the current plan's proposal for diploma release for all graduating seniors needs to be revised to exclude those seven students.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical capacity issue. I confirmed with the civic auditorium yesterday that the fire marshal approval limits each ceremony session to 450 people. We have 286 graduates, and the current draft's three-ticket-per-graduate plan would produce 858 attendees — well over the 450-person limit. This venue capacity constraint has not yet been added to the event worksheet, and the plan will need to be revised to account for it.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a language access issue. I completed family confirmations this week, and they show that interpretation is required in both Spanish and Somali for graduation announcements and instructions. These language requests have not yet been added to the ceremony plan, so the current draft's English-only announcements will need to be revised to include Spanish and Somali interpretation.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical safety and legal issue. I verified in the student-services file that there is a current court order prohibiting contact between two graduating students. This means they must be assigned to separate ceremony sessions and must use separate arrival and departure entrances. This court order has not yet been attached to the ceremony seating plan, and the current draft — which proposes one ceremony with general seating by homeroom — does not account for this separation requirement. The plan will need to be revised to include multiple ceremony sessions and separate entrance logistics for these two students.
